text:
maya (Support): quick escalation — multiple ACME users are hitting 403s on the console and via API after the nightly SSO/SCIM sync (~18:22 UTC). Customer reports ~12 people affected, all in the Okta group 'ACME Developers'.

maya (Support): Symptoms:
- Console: '403 Permission denied' when opening project 'acme-prod' settings and listing models.
- API: calls to /v1/projects/acme-prod/models return 403 with body below.
- Okta SCIM logs show group provisioning success but our role mapping appears unchanged.

maya (Support): Repro steps I ran:
1) Sign in as affected user via SSO -> console shows spinner then 403.
2) Grabbed the session cookie and hit API: `curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/projects/acme-prod/models`
3) Response: 
```
{"error":"PermissionDenied","status":403,"message":"User does not have project:read role for project 'acme-prod'"}
```

maya (Support): I created internal ticket SUP-2026-413 and notified account team. Assigning SRE/eng because this smells like role mapping mismatch after org cleanup. @devon @alan can you take a look? :eyes:

okta-bot: SCIM provisioning event for group 'ACME Developers' -> processed (18:21:55 UTC). mappedGroups: ['ACME Developers'] action: upsert membershipCount: 14

jenna (Org Admin): FYI we changed a role label two days ago — renamed internal role 'developer' -> 'dev' to match new naming convention. I updated the console UI to show 'dev' but didn't touch the Okta mapping (I thought SCIM handles it).

devon (SRE): That would explain it. Our authz layer expects the role slug 'developer' in the org.role_mappings used by the SCIM adapter. If Okta is still sending group -> 'developer' but our code maps to 'dev' now, mismatch could drop memberships.

alan (Eng:auth): Can you paste the org.role_mappings for acme-org? I want to see what the mapping table contains. Also need the exact SCIM payload.

maya (Support): Pasting relevant bits from the SCIM event and a couple logs: 
```
SCIM event: {"groupName":"ACME Developers","members":["u1","u2","u3"],"externalMappings":[{"role":"developer","project":"acme-prod"}]}

Authz check log: 2026-03-15T18:22:03Z authz: check user:u2 org:acme-org project:acme-prod -> role lookup failed for slug 'developer' -> result DENY (403)
```

alan (Eng:auth): Confirmed — our DB has role entries: ['admin','dev','viewer'] for acme-org. There is no 'developer' slug. So SCIM payload still references the old slug 'developer'.

devon (SRE): Two vectors: 1) fix Okta SCIM app to send 'dev' instead of 'developer'; 2) accept both slugs in the role mapping service for a short period (backfill). We should do 2) first so customer access is restored quickly.

jenna (Org Admin): I can push a temporary group mapping from Okta side but that requires a change request and takes ~30-60 min depending on approvals. I'd prefer eng hotfix then a proper Okta update.

alan (Eng:auth): I can ship a tiny patch to our mapping service to treat 'developer' as alias to 'dev'. Quick pseudo-patch: 
```
// mapping alias handling
if (role_slug not found) {
  alias = alias_table.lookup(role_slug)
  if (alias) role_slug = alias
}
// alias_table contains {"developer":"dev"}
```
I'll also add an audit log entry so we can undo later.

devon (SRE): After alan's patch, I'll run a backfill to reconfirm members are granted the project role again. Backfill plan: query recent SCIM events where role != mapped role and reapply grants.

maya (Support): In the meantime I applied manual project role assignments for 2 lead engineers so ACME can get unblocked. They confirmed console access restored. Still need org-wide fix. I've messaged the customer (ACME IT) with a short note and ETA ~30m.

deploy-bot: deploy started by alan (Eng:auth) for service 'role-mapper' commit ab12c3d -> staging -> prod (canary).

alan (Eng:auth): Deployed patch to prod canary at 18:40 UTC. Rolling forward. Patch adds alias for 'developer' -> 'dev' and logs.

devon (SRE): Backfill running now against SCIM events from last 48h. Running in dry-run first, then apply. Progress: 0/14 users reconciled (dry-run).

devon (SRE): Backfill applied, granting project:read to 12 users. Repro check: curl returns 200 and list of models now.
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
{"models":[{"id":"m-1","name":"eng-prototype"}, ...]}
```

maya (Support): Customer updated: "Looks good, team can access again. Please confirm root cause and permanent fix." They asked for timeline for Okta change.

alan (Eng:auth): Root cause summary for customer: during an org cleanup we renamed internal role slug 'developer' -> 'dev' but the Okta SCIM configuration still referenced the old slug. SCIM events referenced a non-existent role slug so our mapper dropped the grants which resulted in 403s. Temporary fix: added alias handling and backfilled grants. Permanent next steps: update Okta SCIM mapping to use 'dev' and remove alias after 2 weeks.

jenna (Org Admin): I'll open the Okta change request and coordinate the push with ACME IT. Will include a request for a SCIM resync once the mapping is updated.

maya (Support): Action items: 
- alan: revert/remove alias after 2026-03-29 if no issues (and note in changelog).
- devon: monitor authz errors and run audit job for 48h.
- jenna: coordinate Okta mapping update and resync.
- maya: send detailed RCA to ACME and close SUP-2026-413 once customer ack.

maya (Support): Marking support thread resolved for now since customer confirmed access restored. Leaving open until Okta mapping change is confirmed by jenna. :thumbsup:

devon (SRE): I'll watch logs for spikes and ping here if anything reoccurs.

okta-bot: SCIM resync requested by jenna (Org Admin) for app 'ACME SCIM' at 19:05 UTC.

maya (Support): Thanks all — nice triage and fast patching.
